title: Five loaves by the lake (Matthew 14:1–21)
hook: why does a story about feeding a crowd begin at a grave?
tomorrow: why do you start to sink the second you look down?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a storeroom with room for both, and a hometown with room only for the old. New and old. Today, a hard day by the lake.

You've had awful news and you just want to be alone. Then your phone lights up: someone else needs you, right now. Matthew has a story that sits exactly there, and it comes with a puzzle. Why does a picnic for thousands start with a death? A gentle warning for anyone listening with kids: it's told in one short line. John, the man who baptized Jesus, has been killed in prison by Herod the tetrarch. His friends bury him and come to tell Jesus.
screen: `AWFUL NEWS, AND A BUZZING PHONE.` → `A PICNIC THAT STARTS AT A GRAVE.` → `JOHN IS DEAD.`

segments.voice: Matthew's next line: "When Jesus heard of it, he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart." Apart. Away from everyone. But the crowds hear where he's gone and follow on foot, and when he lands, the quiet place is full. Here's the hinge: "And Jesus went forth, and saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and he healed their sick." Nothing says the grief is over. The compassion comes anyway. By evening, the disciples have a sensible plan: send everyone off to buy food. He says: "They need not depart; give ye them to eat." Their answer: "We have here but five loaves, and two fishes." He has the people sit on the grass, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks, and gives the bread to the disciples, and the disciples give it to the crowd. Notice whose hands carry it: the friends who wanted to send everyone home. And the ending: "they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full." So, the puzzle. Why open a feast at a grave? Matthew sets them side by side, with no gap between. On the same day, in the same person, grief and compassion share the room. One doesn't have to finish before the other begins.
screen: `A DESERT PLACE APART.` · `MOVED WITH COMPASSION ANYWAY.` · `GIVE YE THEM TO EAT.` · `GRIEF AND COMPASSION, ONE DAY.`

segments.voice: Name one person who could use something from you this week. Then name what might stop you: a low mood, a long day, your own sad news. Now choose the smallest version you could still give on a hard day, five loaves rather than a banquet, and hold that plan while you breathe.
Five loaves by the lake. Not much to start with, broken and handed out by the disciples, on the day John was buried.
screen: `FIVE LOAVES BY THE LAKE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: compassion in grief. Sadness doesn't have to clear the room before kindness walks in. Take care.

howItsDone: Some churches bring meals to grieving families, and some Christians say grace before meals with thanks for the hands that brought the food, remembering loaves broken and shared.

fork.reveal: Jesus withdrew apart first, and then, seeing the crowd, was moved with compassion. in Matthew, grief and compassion share the same day; neither cancels the other.

chat.says: Pop's best friend Mr. Hollis died. Pop's up at 6 making potato salad for the family. shouldn't he rest?
options: Let him, and help. Grief and compassion can share a day. Offer to carry the bowl over.
Make him stay home. You can't care for anybody until you've finished grieving yourself.
He's dodging his feelings. Tell him to stop cooking and just sit with the loss instead.
chat.meaning: Grieving John, Jesus went apart, then saw the crowd and was moved with compassion. In Matthew, grief and kindness share the same day.

Herod the tetrarch.meaning: a ruler over part of the land under Rome

notes: Hard scene: John's death (14:3–12) is told in one restrained line, with a gentle warning for listeners with children; the beheading, Herodias and her daughter are not named. Confirm the restraint is right.
'A picnic for thousands' rests on 14:21 (about five thousand men, besides women and children).

Matthew 14:13 does not give a motive for withdrawing; the voice says 'Apart. Away from everyone' and 'Nothing says the grief is over' as a reading of the scene. The index hook calls it grief. Confirm.
Puzzle shape: the answer (Matthew sets grief and compassion side by side) is an interpretation of the order of events, not a claim about Matthew's intent. Confirm.
'Some readers hear ... the Last Supper' (Matthew 26:26) is hedged and appears only in the trapdoor; confirm.

Grace storyline day 9: Pop's oldest friend from church, Mr. Hollis, has died; Pop is still cooking for the family. This begins a slower thread of Pop's grief through 1456. Pacing note: no quick recovery.
